A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same class-aware contrastive-learning work despite changes to the title and method name. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Both contain eight main-text pages followed by references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection experiments across four datasets, including method comparisons, component ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds MANTA, COCOAD, 3D evaluation, model-transfer comparisons and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: LGC is renamed CCL, but class-aware sampling, the four-block projector, local feature matching, global contrastive learning and the combined training objective remain unchanged. Applications to additional models and 3D data do not document a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds MANTA with 38 categories, COCOAD with 81 categories and MVTec 3D-AD, substantially expanding coverage and introducing 3D evaluation. The original four datasets remain, and the all-in-all comparison still combines only those four datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RLR to the original comparison methods. The transfer comparisons expand from four one-for-one reconstruction models to include original-versus-CCL results for ViTAD, MambaAD and CRD, covering additional model families. AST and M3DM are mentioned without corresponding reported comparison rows.

E3.justification: The added COCOAD evaluation reports image- and pixel-level mAP and maximum F1 alongside AUROC and PRO. Computational comparisons introduce FLOPs. The retained experiments preserve the stated input resolution, batch size, optimizer, learning rates and early-stopping procedure.

E4.justification: The applicability analysis now tests whether CCL benefits existing one-for-all architectures and a 3D reconstruction model, with computational-overhead comparisons. The one-layer MLP ablation and several visualization cases, including all VISA examples, are removed. The new component-summary table largely consolidates results already reported in v1.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without explicit seed or uncertainty information. v2 Table 1 states that standard deviations across five random seeds are below 0.1 for CCL's three all-in-all metrics. This is newly reported uncertainty information, not evidence that the run count increased.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for MANTA, COCOAD, model transfer, 3D detection and computational costs. In the retained all-in-all setting, Table 1 changes CCL's I-AUROC/P-AUROC/PRO from 90.6/97.8/90.5 to 90.6/97.9/90.6, although Section 4.2 retains the old values. The KC=30 pseudo-label PRO also changes from 91.3 to 91.4.

T1.justification: The mathematical setting and Equations 1–6 retain the same definitions, feature-matching rule and loss formulations. Neither version supplies theorem or proof material, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list narrow the central problem from catastrophic forgetting plus inter-class confusion to inter-class confusion. v2 also adds a headline contribution claiming potential to enhance existing one-for-all models and extend to 3D anomaly detection, substantially broadening the stated applicability.

C2.justification: v1's limitation reporting slightly worse adaptations of CRAD and UniAD is omitted; v2 reports successful adaptations of different models, ViTAD and MambaAD. v2 adds unsatisfactory generalization to unseen data and explains marginal SimpleNet/CFlow gains through a proposed need for joint classifier optimization. These revise important applicability boundaries and mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: Figure 3c adds a detailed projector/neck schematic, and Table 4 supplies per-model FLOP costs, including RD's increase from 28.4 to 30.7 G. Most implementation settings and the project website are retained. The additional experiments receive relatively little configuration detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new datasets and model comparisons, alongside newer work such as Dinomaly, and removes HVQ-Trans and several background citations. The related-work organization and principal positioning around reconstruction methods and class-aware contrastive learning remain similar.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, method name, authorship and affiliations, polishes prose, and combines or reorders ablation discussions. The overall section structure and much of the introduction and method exposition remain closely aligned with v1.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces the domain-shift panel with detailed architecture information. Result displays are substantially reorganized: COCOAD receives a new table, transfer results gain model groups and FLOP columns, and several ablations become baseline-plus-difference tables. The projector bar chart disappears, while the qualitative figure is reduced from twelve examples to seven and moved to one column.

improvement.justification: The additional COCOAD, 3D and model-transfer experiments strengthen the evidence for applicability, while FLOP measurements and limited seed reporting improve practical and statistical assessment. These gains are moderated by sparse documentation of new experiments, omission of the earlier negative CRAD/UniAD adaptation observations, and reporting inconsistencies such as the disagreement between Table 1 and Section 4.2.
